([[West Palm Beach, Florida]]) | college = [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]] (2015–2017) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = * First-team All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] (2017) | medaltemplates = }} '''John Martin Collins III''' (born September 23, 1997) is an American professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest Demon Deacons]]. ==Early years== Collins was born in [[Layton, Utah]]. He attended [[Cardinal Newman High School (West Palm Beach, Florida)|Cardinal Newman High School]] in [[West Palm Beach, Florida]]. While at Newman, Collins was a three-time letter winner and was named the Florida Class 4A Player of the Year his senior year. On November 13, 2014, he signed a letter of intent to play college basketball at [[Wake Forest University|Wake Forest]].{{cite web|title=Wake Forest Signs Three to Letters of Intent|url=http://www.wakeforestsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/111314aaa.html|website=wakeforestsports.com|accessdate=9 March 2017}} ==College career== Collins appeared in all 31 of his team's game during his freshman year. He led the team in field goal percentage at 54.7%. {{cite web|title=Wake Forest Bio|url=http://www.wakeforestsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/john_collins_958538.html|website=wakeforestsports.com|accessdate=9 March 2017}} As a starter his sophomore year, Collins led the team in scoring with 19.2 points per game. His performance earned him recognition as the [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] Most-Improved Player and he as named first-team all-ACC.{{cite web|title=ACC ANNOUNCES ALL-CONFERENCE TEAM, POSTSEASON AWARDS|url=http://www.theacc.com/news/acc-announces-all-conference-team-postseason-awards-03-05-2017|website=theacc.com|accessdate=9 March 2017}} After the season Collins entered the [[2017 NBA Draft]], forgoing his final two years of eligibility.{{cite web|last1=Associated Press|title=Wake's John Collins to remain in NBA draft|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2017/04/12/wakes-john-collins-to-remain-in-nba-draft/100403300/|website=USAToday.com|accessdate=18 April 2017}} ==Personal life== John's parents are John Collins Jr. and Lyria Rissing-Collins. His parents were both in the military and as a result, the family moved a lot during Collins' youth.{{cite web|last1=Johns|first1=Les|title=Mother and mentor guide John Collins' path to success|url=http://www.scout.com/college/wake-forest/story/1749746-championship-edge|website=Scout.com|accessdate=9 March 2017|date=27 January 2017}} == References == {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[http://www.wakeforestsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/john_collins_958538.html Wake Forest bio] *[http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/John-Collins-76415/ DraftExpress.com profile] {{DEFAULTSORT:Collins, John}} [[Category:1997 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Basketball players from Florida]] [[Category:Power forwards (basketball)]] [[Category:Sportspeople from West Palm Beach, Florida]] [[Category:Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball players]]
